quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash?

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders are most likely to crash. They lack training and are unfamiliar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, rain, and cold.
Take artificial stimulants.
Limit how far you ride in one day.
Take frequent breaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Never use artificial stimulants because when they wear off, the effects can be very dangerous.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it hard.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely and right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: Where should you ride so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left side of the lane.
In the right side of the lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride behind the car in the center of your lane. This position places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to see you. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Alcohol leaves your body faster.
The effects of alcohol are less noticeable.
You are more likely to avoid being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, more of it builds up in your body. Never operate a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect its balance.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sturdy boots.
Tennis shoes.
Shoes with loose laces.
Sandals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots work best. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to handle differently?

options.text: Continue riding normally.
Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you feel the handling change, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, what should they do?

options.text: Pass in pairs.
Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.
Pass one at a time.
Avoid passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time on a two-lane road. Each rider should finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Communicate your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Search for hazards in your path.
Hope the other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope the other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, communicate your intentions, and stay alert for hazards. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you. Be prepared to react to anything.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors like red, orange, yellow, and green make you more visible. Dark colors like black are harder to see.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear clothing that is tight.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers must wear helmets and lean with the operator during turns. Loose clothing should be avoided. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Use your turn signals to indicate that you plan to change lanes.
Tailgate other drivers.
Keep your eyes focused no more than 15 feet in front of your motorcycle.
Not use a headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals to indicate that you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Be visible, communicate your intentions, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the new rider to lead.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: There is a hissing noise coming from the rear of the bike.
The back end is jerking from side to side.
You are unable to accelerate.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end is jerking from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually cannot hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by your right foot.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding alongside another vehicle?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. If a hazard appears, you have no escape route. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not be used.
Should not balloon when riding.
Are not needed since motorcycles should not be ridden in the rain.
Should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits made for motorcycles will not tear or puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: To get the best protection, your helmet should:

options.text: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
Look sturdy.
Be inexpensive.
Be in your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other drivers and helps them see you. Stay out of another driver's blind spot for long periods of time.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should:

options.text: Sit on the motorcycle seat.
Sit in the sidecar.
Sit either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not sit on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the sidecar.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Give you an escape route.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe by keeping you out of blind spots, helping you see and be seen, helping you avoid hazards and wind from other vehicles, and giving you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Often
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles is a better sign of tire failure.

questions.question: The center portion of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Most accidents happen.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is where debris and oil from cars collect. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found in the center of the lane.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Others may drive slowly while looking for a parking spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve:

options.text: Only use the front brake.
It will work the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it takes care. Your tires are already using traction to make the turn while leaning, so less traction is available for braking.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you talk to each other.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. This limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: It is not serious.
You cannot change direction.
It will fix itself.
It only matters if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash or serious injury. When the rear wheel locks up, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: How should you make a quick stop on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on wet surfaces. The front brake is safe if you apply it slowly to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Stay alert because another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed up this process. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle wobbles?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make a wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and move your weight forward and down. Pull over as soon as possible.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes. This cuts your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you see when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible. You may see a small part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at night.
They are caused by bald tires.
They occur at speeds above 55 mph.
They involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, be visible to others by using signals and positioning your motorcycle correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle and scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be prepared to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. Brake slowly only on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what is usually safest?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder of the road to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, ride straight within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center portion of your lane.
In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
Move between all three portions of your lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It applies partial rear braking when the front brake is used.
It applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
It applies the same braking force to both brakes when either is used.
It learns and remembers your braking habits.

questions.correctAnswerText: It applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: Which of these provides good protection for a motorcyclist?

options.text: A jacket that leaves your arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that do not cover your ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels that will not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves or gloves made from other durable materials protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: What should a good face shield do?

options.text: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be too tight for glasses to fit underneath.
Not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Long-term cold weather riding can cause all of the following except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Long-term cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from cold weather.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator prevent other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center portion of your lane leaves less space on both sides of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing down or stopping.
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads.
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency.
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: You should always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.
